1.why: All text uses a clean sans-serif with visible letter spacing and ample line height, though it appears to be a standard family rather than a specifically dyslexia-friendly typeface.

2.why: No italics, all-caps strings, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; every message is a short single-line sentence.

3.why: The single-column mobile-width layout is readable, but in steps 2-8 up to eight identical error banners stack up, creating clutter and pushing the form down the page.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Sign in to start your security setup.' and 'Use your saved password' are short and written in plain language.

5.why: The email field shows 'Example: marcus@example.com', but the password field only gets a hint and no code-entry screen with an example is ever shown.

6.why: The longest content is the two-line demo sign-in note; the user is never required to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere and the flow never reaches the OTP or recovery-code screens where long codes would exist.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is present in any of the eight screenshots.

9.why: Standard labeled email/password inputs plus the 'Use your saved password' hint suggest password-manager support, though autocomplete markup cannot be verified from images.

10.why: 'Step 1 of 4 · Sign in' marks the position and the full-width blue 'Sign in' button is the clear primary action, although the stack of red banners competes for attention.

11.why: Each screen requests a single main action via one 'Sign in' button, with 'Need help?' offered only as a collapsed secondary disclosure.

12.why: After each attempt the only feedback is another copy of the same generic error banner; nothing plainly states what happened or what comes next, and a successful outcome is never shown.

13.why: Sign-in can be retried repeatedly with entered values preserved and no visible lockout, but no reveal, hide, or re-request controls for codes exist in the observed flow.

14.why: 'Check your email and password, then try again.' is neutral in tone and names the problem area and the fix, though it does not specify which field failed.

15.why: No countdown, timeout, or time pressure appears on any screen, but the code-entry step was never reached so generous code-entry time could not be confirmed.
